newsitem.title: UK: Study cites low support for European integration.
newsitem.headline: Study cites low support for European integration.

text.p: Many Europeans support the concept of European integration, but fewer and fewer back the idea on a concrete level, a British trade body said on Tuesday.
The Market Research Society said these were the results of a study done recently for the European Commission, the European Union's executive body.
"Public support for further European integration is at an all time low throughout Europe despite the fact that support in principal for a unified Europe has never been stronger," the society said.
The Market Research Society said the findings of the study would be published by Karlheinz Reif, an adviser to the European Commission, at the society's annual conference in Birmingham on Friday.

It said Reif's study showed so-called Euro-pessimists across northern Europe objected to further European integration for political reasons, while Euro-pessimists in southern Europe gave mostly economic reasons.

"Those countries which have recently joined the (European) Union have a lower than average enthusiasm for Europe, very much in line with the attitudes of Denmark, Ireland and the UK just after they joined the Union in 1973," the Market Research Society said in a statement.

The society said it was interested in attitudes about European integration because Britain's market research industry had a 22-percent share of the total European market research business worth about 536 million pounds ($850.4 million).
It said Reif was adviser to the European Commission's director general for Information and Communication.
